coaching.headline: Eight towers to none, every big major on the board against only two seedlings for them, and four won fights cashed four for four: the blueprint game.
coaching.team: Our pre-game read called four of five lanes theirs. The map disagreed, because we only fought where our objectives were. The leak first: three solo deaths between 8.7 and 15, Shinbi to Khaimera, Phase to Kira, and Renna to Khaimera. That was the one pattern that survived the win. Everything else was a conversion clinic. The fight at our Mini Prime at 12.7 was won 2-0. The fight at our Fangtooth at 17.1 was won 3-0 with two of ours against three. The fight at our inhibitor at 24.6 was won 3-1, and the fight at 26.7 was won 2-1. Every single win was cashed inside the window. Their only won fight, at our inner tower at 18.8 and taken while Greystone and Renna stayed in lane, cashed into nothing. The major board was all ours: Fangtooth at 10 and 17. A third Fangtooth followed at 24. Mini Prime came at 14, Genesis Core at 20. Orb Prime followed at 22. Only the seedlings, at 4 and 11, went theirs. Zero majors were conceded, and not one of our deaths preceded a lost structure. One draft note to carry forward: our damage was four-fifths magical, so a single enemy magic-resist item blunts most of it, and a tougher lobby will buy one. Next game: same rule that won this one — fight at our objectives, cash every win before the timers end.
coaching.whatShiftedIt: The fight at our Fangtooth at 17.1: Renna and GRIM.exe, two against Kira, Aurora and Khaimera, won it 3-0, with Fangtooth taken at 17 in the same window. From that double prize the rest cascaded — Genesis Core, Orb Prime, a third Fangtooth, and the 8-0 tower count.

The catch by Khaimera at 15 was the lone bad minute.

7c8ab99c-31c5-4ea5-a6fa-e0d6417c3f1b.text: A support lane that read losing on paper, and the first Fangtooth at 10 still went our way behind 16,399 healing.

coaching.whatWorked: The discipline to fight only where our own objectives stood: Mini Prime, Fangtooth, the inhibitor. Every win was cashed inside the window, four for four, and nothing on the major board was conceded all game. Objective-anchored fight selection is the blueprint to repeat.

17.1.call: The ground did the work: on our own Fangtooth, they had to cross the map and engage into a set position. The one wrinkle is that it was taken two-strong. The identical setup with a third body rotated in turns a great win into a guaranteed take.

24.6.call: Standing on the inhibitor rather than ceding it was the right call, and defending under our own structure is why a thin fight held. Still, two bodies against a four-man push is a coin-flip. When the base is the target, the shove-and-rotate from every other lane has to be automatic.

12.7.call: This was the template: meet them at our own Mini Prime, let the objective anchor the fight, and walk away with both the kills and the prize. Nothing to change here — this is the read to run back at every spawn timer.

7c8ab99c-31c5-4ea5-a6fa-e0d6417c3f1b.build: Mr_Meat31's Phase was on core and it showed: Enra's Blessing auto-shields a nearby ally the moment they get stunned or rooted, Galaxy Greaves bring both resist types with movement speed, and Marshal gives her something to do between saves. Windcaller, the one off-list pick, still fits the kit, granting a burst of movement speed to Phase and whoever she boosts, more fuel for repositioning the carry. With 16,399 health healed in a game where all 4 won fights were cashed, this is a support build doing its job.
7c8ab99c-31c5-4ea5-a6fa-e0d6417c3f1b.eternal: Vesh is the aggressive read on Phase: her damaging abilities leave a burn behind, so even a support's poke keeps ticking, and The Tenth Seal strengthens her level-10 ultimate. Mind Rot lets the chip damage bother frontliners. The trade is real on a healer: it does nothing for her heals or shields, so the loadout leans on her link and her item choices to do the protecting while the blessing adds teeth.

16f28434-561f-4f23-9454-40321f4a1ef3.build: Goldilocks324 bent GRIM.exe toward abilities: Nuclear Rounds boosts ability damage, Necrosis speeds up and strengthens the ultimate, and Overseer amplifies damage while healing back a cut of it. The listed core goes the other way, Lightning Hawk and Dust Devil stacking attack speed and slows around Plasma Blade's crit ramp. At 6 kills, 1 death, and 27,351 hero damage in a win, the ability-leaning version answered fine; the trade it made was steady basic-attack pressure for bigger ultimate moments, and this game those moments kept landing.
16f28434-561f-4f23-9454-40321f4a1ef3.eternal: Vermis rewards the basic-attack half of GRIM.exe: every third hit on one target bites for max-health damage, Serration finishes low targets, and Melting Point keeps armor stackers honest. That suits an enemy front that stacked health and armor around Scarlett and Khaimera. What it trades is synergy with the ability-heavy build he actually ran; the blessing pays on sustained shooting, so weaving attacks between casts is how both halves get their value.

a0c393cc-1437-4bdc-8168-64676ce2166c.build: Cuban Noobster's Greystone deviated once and the deviation was the team's anti-heal: Tainted Guard cuts the healing of whoever hits him, aimed straight at a Khaimera who healed 12,365 health by swinging into people. Around it sat the proper frame, Overlord's permanent health stacking and Aegis Of Agawar's armor that swells at low health. Rapture, the skipped piece, adds on-hit damage and lifesteal for longer duels; on a 3-kill, 0-death game with 32,690 damage absorbed, nothing about the trade needs apologizing for.
a0c393cc-1437-4bdc-8168-64676ce2166c.eternal: Thraex suits Greystone's job of never leaving the fight: the mark makes his current target hit him softer while he hits them harder, compounding his armor items, and Ferocity's stacking attack speed grows with every second he refuses to die. Savage Strikes adds on-hit damage so the tank still threatens. The trade-off is that it is all one-target dueling; it does less in scattered teamfights where he swaps targets, which is where his area damage and revive already carry him.

a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e.build: Xeebs ran Renna's full core, Entropy, Wraith Leggings, and Overseer, then stacked Oblivion Crown on top, which multiplies her total magic power. Overseer remains the pivot piece: more damage on everything, a share of it healed back. Five kills on 21,295 hero damage into the enemy's biggest source, Neon's 23k magical, is the mid matchup going our way; the comp flag is the one caution, since our damage was 4/5 magical and one enemy magic-resist item blunts most of it, which makes Wraith Leggings' penetration the most load-bearing buy in the build.
a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e.eternal: Vesh stacks with Renna's poke: every landed ability leaves a growing burn, so the harassment she wins mid with keeps working after she backs off. Mind Rot gives the burn teeth against beefier targets and The Tenth Seal boosts the level-10 ultimate. The cost is the usual mage bargain, no defensive help at all; into Neon's long-range magical damage it is a bet that Renna out-pokes rather than out-lasts.

10edbf65-457d-48d0-9151-9df5b4fcb40a.build: Willy Guggenheim's Shinbi had the ability core mostly right: Spirit Of Amir gives magic lifesteal inside the jungle, Oathkeeper adds an empowered strike after every cast, and Magnify, the stand-in for Wraith Leggings, shreds magic armor with each spell instead of flatly piercing it, with omnivamp and health besides. That swap is defensible on a diving jungler. The flag was not: no armor against a three-physical lineup, and 46,956 damage taken, the heaviest load on the team, says an armor piece was the missing buy.
10edbf65-457d-48d0-9151-9df5b4fcb40a.eternal: Vesh matches Shinbi's caster rhythm: her wolves and dashes are all ability damage, and each hit leaves a burn that keeps working while she repositions. Mind Rot aims that burn at durable targets, and The Tenth Seal loads up the level-10 ultimate that headlines her teamfights. What it forgoes is the on-hit style her attack-speed windows could use, and any toughness for the dive itself.

loadout.name: RAM
loadout.text: Gain 5 Magical Power and 25% Base Mana Regen on takedown, stacking infinitely. At 3 stacks gain 5% Movement Speed. Upon death, lost 50% of stacks rounded up.
